body:
Application
Age: 15
Timezone: Central
Do you have access to TeamSpeak? Yes/No: Yes
Do you have access to Skype? Yes/No: Yes
Do you have access to a recording software? Yes/No: Yes

CRITERIA 1: SELF REFLECTION/EVALUATION

Do you have any experience as a staff member on any servers?
Yes, I have previously run a server of my own. It was not a large server, it consisted of myself and some friends, and was eventually and briefly opened to the public, but I was still able to get some experience from it. I was the head of staff there, ran most other staff, and organized most events. Since then, I have retired from that server, and haven't played on it for a long time.

What is your biggest weakness and how do you believe it will affect your moderating? What is your biggest strength and how would this affect your moderating?
My biggest weakness is most likely that I would be slow with punishments compared to other staff members. I do not have the fastest software and may take longer than others to get evidence of the person I need to punish, and I would want to make sure I have everything correct (spelling, reason, etc) before actually giving them the infraction. Another weakness of mine is that I can sometimes take things not as serious as they should be. Most of the time, I'm good with realizing when things are serious compared to when they are meant to be fun or messing around, but there are times when I struggle to know when to transition from one to the other. My biggest strength is that I'm able to not be biased towards others. I believe that rules are rules. Even if I like someone, or dislike someone, I would give them the same punishment as anybody else, not more harsh, or less harsh. I am also somebody who many people enjoy to be around talk to, and can help others with many of their problems if I am come to.

How do you believe you can help improve the Staff Team?
I have realized I am online a lot of the time where there are no staff members online. I believe I can help by being active while others are not. I am also a very social person and enjoy meeting new people, so I would contribute to the staff team by being somebody who people want to be around. I enjoy being around others and want the server to be a better place in general. Along with that, I can act as somebody who is impartial to a situation and give my say on it. Throughout my life I have made the rule for myself to at least stay neutral with everybody I meet. I may not like the person, but I try to not dislike the person, and treat them fairly. I would apply this rule to when I moderate on the server, as I do for my life. Finally, I am a friendly person in general, who is willing to make new friends, or just hang around. I love to make jokes and will do almost anything to make somebody laugh. 

What qualities does a leader need to have in your opinion? Do you consider yourself to be a leader? Why?
In my opinion, a leader needs to be able to make decisions on his/her own. These decisions should not only be made for them, but for the group of people they lead. A leader should be willing to put others before them, and represent the group he/she is the leader of, as well as listen to others' opinions. I personally do not consider myself a leader, but many others have in the past and present. Others have said I care for others over myself, which I agree with. I would rather see others enjoy themselves over myself, and would rather help somebody else over helping myself. I do not consider myself a leader because I would rather simply be a person in the group. I do not want to be looked at as somebody who is over others, and would rather just fit in. I have organized things in the past for many of my social groups, and have had the final say in things, but I never do those things thinking I am a leader, I simply do them because that is what I believe is right, and it follows my morals to do those things. One of the times I've stood out as a "leader" for the community is when I made a forum post about using the term "beaner". I am Caucasian, but I still knew a large portion of the community are Hispanic, and I disagree with using racial slurs. I was able to speak up for the community and change the rules to better the server by doing so.

What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?
Some of the main attributes distinguishing me from other players are the following. I try to make things as easy as possible for the staff team currently. I use /report rather than screaming about it in public chat, and most of the time I use /report, I have left the game to make sure the person is hacking (or doing whatever I report them for), before reporting them as to not waste a staff member's time on somebody who is clean. I am also not somebody who will bend rules for others. In my opinion, the rules are the rules. Even if somebody were to apologize for something, and they are sincerely sorry for what they did, they still broke the rules in a way, so they should be punished. If they are not punished for what they did, they may get the idea that they can just apologize for anything they do, and get away with it. If people are not punished for what they do, I believe they will not learn their lesson from it. I also do not enjoy when players are toxic towards others, and try to avoid it, rather than add on to it. If somebody or a group of people are being toxic to another, they should be stopped, instead of encouraged by other people to take it further. I am a very social person who is able to put many things into words and explain things that are difficult for most people to explain. I enjoy talking to and meeting new people, and hope to do so, along with be more active than I already am, if I get accepted. I actually want to go into psychology as a career as an adult, so I already know a lot about how people react socially to certain situations. It also means I really want to pursue helping others, and making things right for people. I have also played many sports, and through those I have learned how important it is to have good communication with others, along with working with your team, rather than against it while trying to take the glory for yourself. Along with playing sport I have received a large amount of constructive criticism. Because of this, I am willing to listen to what other staff and my mentor may say about my abilities as a staff member, and try to improve on myself, rather than ignore it, or get angry about it.

What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community? Do you believe you have these skills?
I believe I should be able to cleanly communicate and talk to others in the community. Along with understanding the viewpoint of another in a situation, rather than only looking at your own side of things. In order to interact with the community, you should be able to be respectful of people, and treat them nicely, even if you do not like said person very much. I believe I most all of these skills. I am a very affable person, and many other people have told me I am as well. I enjoy helping others, and like to hear both sides of the story before making a decision on things. I will admit I am very shy when first meeting new people, but once I know how to be social with them, I am very social with them. Along with once I'm introduced to one person in a group, I am able to be introduced to the others in the group much more easily than the original person.

How much time can you commit to being a staff member (Rough Idea)? 
I can most likely commit at least an hour every day on weekdays with school, but much more on weekend days or when there is no school.

CRITERIA 2: GENERAL SITUATIONS

You are currently undergoing your junior moderator trial. A ban evader is online and he is constantly ban evading and hacking. You are the only one online and the only one who is able to be online. What would you do?
I would gather enough evidence of the hacker, enough to have them punished. Afterwards, I would freeze them and try to get another staff member to have them punished. I would hope another staff member could come online possibly with pixelchat or another way to ban them permanently. 

Another staff member is constantly joining and harassing other people on Teamspeak in their team channel. The staff member is also referee and has physical permissions to be in that channel. However the leaders do not want this staff member in there and they have asked him to leave multiple times. What would you do?
I would first poke them and ask them to stop harassing the people in the channel. If they continue, I would move them from the channel into a channel I am in. There I would discuss with him/her other possibilities of how this problem could be resolved, in efforts to get them to stop. If they persist to do this, I would contact a senior staff member and report this issue to them so they can punish him/her properly.

A player appeals a punishment you gave them. You realize that the evidence file is corrupted and therefore there is no physical evidence. You know however this person did indeed break the rules, what would you do?
Because I do not have evidence, the player would have their punishment appealed. Unfortunately there is nothing I would be able to do about this. But I would let other staff members know to keep an eye out for the player and watch for him/her to do what originally gave him the infraction again. I would also most likely watch the player myself in times where we are both on and no other reports are sent in, even without a report sent in on them.

You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confident but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?
If my team mate were to put information meant for other staff members into our team discord, I would first confront them about this problem. I would tell them I have to report them to the senior staff, and apologize about the whole situation. Afterward, I would contact senior staff, reporting the person to them for leaking information, and allow for them to punish them accordingly.

One day the Senior Staff team makes a decision you do not agree with. You do not know all the details of the decision or the circumstances in which they were made and you were simply told by another staff member. However you do not like the decision based from what you know. What would you do?
I would first contact senior staff or whoever was the person who originally made the decision. I would find all the details behind the decision, and depending on them, react in a different way. If the details made it change my thoughts to support the decision made, I would let the senior staff know I agree with their decision. If I still disagree with the decision, I would also contact senior staff. I would let them know my thoughts about the situation, and possibly recommend changes to their decision, but also allow for them to know I respect their decision, and realize in the end, it is for them to decide upon. I would especially make sure to allow them to know I am not forcing my opinion onto them, just offering suggestions for possible changes for the better.

CRITERIA 3: OTHER
NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.


What would getting moderator on Avicus mean to you?
It would give me a good reason to be more active on Avicus, which is something I've been wanting to do. I want to be able to indulge myself in the community more, and this would help allow me to do so. It would also let me learn new things about teamwork, leadership, and management of a community. Getting moderator on Avicus for me is like being elected into the student government body, meaning I can make decisions for a group of people to better them. 

How passionate are you about Avicus? What does Avicus mean to you?
Avicus has always been the server I go to when I don't know what to play. I first joined when it was only wallsmc, and I played on mczone, and now Avicus. I have met an amazing group of people because of avicus that I still talk to every day, even if they do not play minecraft every day. Avicus is the place where I have met some of the people I trust the most, even if they live across the world, and I love it for that. Besides the people, I have always enjoyed the gamemodes as well. Not many other servers offer a DTM gamemode like avicus does, and I have always preferred Avicus' walls over any other server's.

Do you speak any other languages than English?
I am currently taking Spanish, so I am able to understand a decent amount of it, and I could most likely get by until somebody who is fluent can come. I also started to learn Swedish, but stopped, so I know VERY basic Swedish.

Do you have anything else to add to your application?
I hope to meet and speak to many of the staff members, and even if I am not accepted, still be able to converse with them, and meet new people through this application.
